title: Inexpensive Christmas Tree, but Keep Your Vacuum Handy
text:
Inexpensive Christmas Tree, but Keep Your Vacuum Handy. We are torn in our house when it comes to Christmas decorations. My kids generally want to go all- out, with decorations in every room and on the outside of the house. I tend to get a little less carried away with the season, but I do like Christmas decorations overall and I like having multiple Christmas trees, especially if the trees are different in some important way. This desire for a second tree convinced me to add the Bocca 7 FT Christmas Artificial Pine Tree Full Branches Strong Iron Stand Indoor Outdoor 7FT tree to my home.

This tree arrives in a small box and when I received it, the box seemed too small to hold a seven foot tree. Once I opened the box and started to prepare to assemble, I could see why the box is so small. The tree is narrower than most and there are only four pieces to put together, so it is much easier than other trees to get set up and ready. My current Christmas tree requires inserting each branch separately, so it takes time. With this tree, you just attach the four pieces, spread out the branches, and you’re ready to go.

Spreading out each of the small branches on this tree does take time and once I put everything together, I realized that it would have been better to assemble one piece, then spread out all of the branches first, before moving on to the next. My kids and I were anxious to get it together so we assembled the four pieces first, then started to spread out the branches, which proved to be less efficient.

This tree comes complete with a four- leg stand so it is fairly stable compared to other tree stands I have used over the years, many of which have only three legs. The tree is lightweight, however, so you need to be careful what you place on the branches. As I started to add ornaments, I quickly found that some of them were too heavy and they caused the branches to droop. We will have to save those for our other, green Christmas tree.

Another issue I have had with this tree, and probably its greatest flaw, is the tendency of the needles to fall off. Quite a few were lost upon taking everything out of the box, but more have been lost since then. It makes me question the tree’s quality. I’m hoping that the loss of needles is temporary and the tree won’t lose any more, but I wonder if this will turn out to be true. My other tree doesn’t have any problem like this. Oh well, I guess for a price this low, you can’t expect perfection.

Our holiday décor is growing and expanding each year thanks to overly excited kids and while I think decorations need to be kept in check, I do like the idea of having two trees in the house. This white tree from Bocca is narrower than most trees and thus it can fit into many spaces where other artificial trees will not fit and a white tree is a nice change of pace from the usual green. The quality isn’t the greatest for the reasons stated above, but for a seven foot tall tree, this is a good choice for the price.
